Explain in your own words what 'Entrepreneur Roles and Qualities' refers to.
questions.a: From the French enterprendre, to undertake, the entrepreneur plays three parts at once - innovator bringing new products, organiser assembling the factors of production, and risk bearer shouldering every uncertainty - and does so with initiative, industry knowledge, calculated risk-taking, adaptability, self-confidence and a wealth-creating drive that turns ideas into employment and capital.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Entrepreneur Roles and Qualities'.
questions.a: Innovate, organise, and carry the risk - backed by initiative, adaptability and self-belief, these are the entrepreneur's job description.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Entrepreneur Roles and Qualities' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 13.1 (source: lebt113.txt sections 13.1-13.1.3, Boxes 1-2)

concepts.title: Sources of Funds for New Ventures

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Sources of Funds for New Ventures' refers to.
questions.a: A new venture can be fuelled six ways: the entrepreneur's own personal investment that proves commitment, venture capital chasing high-growth technology plays for equity, angel investors - wealthy field leaders - backing early stages with money and mentorship, business incubators or accelerators that host startups for about two years, government grants and subsidies, and bank loans that demand a solid business plan plus personal guarantee.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Sources of Funds for New Ventures'.
questions.a: Seed money follows conviction - personal funds first, angels and incubators early, venture capital and banks once the plan is proven.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Sources of Funds for New Ventures' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 13.2 Box 3 (source: lebt113.txt section 13.2 Box 3)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Biotech versus General Entrepreneur' refers to.
questions.a: Bio-entrepreneurship weds science to commerce, and the union is demanding: long gestation periods, high capital needs, inherent scientific uncertainty layered on business risk, very high academic qualification and a heavy regulatory framework - the points where a biotech entrepreneur parts ways with the general entrepreneur who shares only competitiveness, teamwork and perseverance.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Biotech versus General Entrepreneur'.
questions.a: Same grit as any founder, plus a laboratory's timeline, budget, regulators and degrees - that is the biotech premium.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Biotech versus General Entrepreneur' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 13.3 (source: lebt113.txt sections 13.3-13.3.2, Table 13.1)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Bharat Biotech Case Study' refers to.
questions.a: Dr Krishna Ella's Bharat Biotech, seeded in Hyderabad in 1997 with angel funds, has shipped over four billion vaccine doses to more than a hundred and twenty developing countries, and its seventeenth vaccine - the inactivated whole-virus COVAXIN - went from bench to India's first indigenous COVID-19 shot in a record eight months, winning WHO emergency use listing since December 2020.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Bharat Biotech Case Study'.
questions.a: Subtract the founding year from the product year to time a company's journey; divide total doses by countries to gauge its reach.

questions.a: years_to_product = product_year - founding_year

concepts.title: IPR and Patent Criteria in Biotechnology

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'IPR and Patent Criteria in Biotechnology' refers to.
questions.a: Intellectual property rights guard biotech innovation under the TRIPS framework: Indian patents rest on the Patents Act 1970, whose Section 5 was deleted by the 2005 amendment to admit product patents in biotechnology, chemicals and pharmaceuticals, and a grant demands novelty, an inventive step that is non-obvious, and utility - never landing in Section 3's negative list or offending public order, with discoveries left unpatentable while inventions qualify.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'IPR and Patent Criteria in Biotechnology'.
questions.a: Novel, non-obvious, useful - and an invention, not a discovery - is the four-point test every biotech patent must pass.

questions.q: Under which section is 'IPR and Patent Criteria in Biotechnology' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 13.4 (source: lebt113.txt sections 13.4-13.4.1)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Biopiracy Cases and Traditional Knowledge' refers to.
questions.a: Biopiracy is the commercial grab of naturally occurring biochemicals or genetic material riding on indigenous knowledge - the neem pesticide patent W R Grace and the USDA took in the 1990s until the EPO revoked it in 2000, the 1995 University of Mississippi turmeric wound-healing patent the CSIR toppled in 1997, and RiceTec's 1997 Basmati claims partly struck down - with India's Traditional Knowledge Digital Library now standing guard at international patent offices.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Biopiracy Cases and Traditional Knowledge'.
questions.a: Old knowledge cannot be a new invention - documented traditional use, TKDL and geographical indications are the shields.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Biopiracy Cases and Traditional Knowledge' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 13.5 (source: lebt113.txt section 13.5)
